I am an old woman now, sixty-five years, and I farm this small piece of land my husband left me. The maize is my food, and I plant cowpea and a little pepper between the stands like my mother showed me. I have no money to buy the fertilizer bag — one bag is too big for my small plot and too dear for my purse, so I carry the goat droppings and the ash from my cooking fire to the field instead. I keep my own seed from last harvest like always, because the improved seed from the dealer in town needs fertilizer to give anything, and I cannot reach that town easy at my age.
